text:
Recent work supports text–ID integration, but offers limited direct evidence for a small text encoder trained entirely from scratch inside NextItNet. Recformer (KDD 2023) combines language and recommendation objectives but initializes from pretrained Longformer; TedRec (CIKM 2024) introduces sequence-level text–ID fusion using pretrained BERT representations. These motivate learning complementary content and interaction features, but their reported gains do not establish effectiveness under the no-pretraining constraint. [Recformer](https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~jmcauley/pdfs/kdd23b.pdf), [TedRec](https://github.com/RUCAIBox/TedRec).

Item specificity and negative selection deserve separate attention. DWSRec (AAAI 2024) finds that anisotropic pretrained text representations hinder item discrimination; this does not demonstrate the same issue in randomly initialized encoders. A 2026 negative-sampling survey emphasizes that difficult unobserved items can be false negatives, making aggressive mining unstable. Semantic similarity alone therefore provides insufficient evidence that an item should receive a strong negative label. [DWSRec](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28786), [negative-sampling survey](https://doi.org/10.1145/3793855).

Practical hypothesis, rather than a verified literature result: preserve NextItNet’s causal dilated residual convolutions and jointly learn a small token-embedding/pooling encoder over titles and truncated descriptions. Fuse its projected output with ID embeddings inside one network, sharing the item representation between history inputs and candidate scoring. Compare titles alone against titles plus descriptions; introduce a modest fraction of text-similar negatives only after a random-negative warm-up, excluding observed training positives. Text can supply shared lexical features, but cannot establish compatibility or purchasing need. Select using the fixed macro validation HR@10. [NextItNet architecture](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf).
